query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a secondary phase or grain refinement through high-pressure torsion (HPT) can overcome the coercivity limitation in single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: High-pressure torsion (HPT) or introduction of a secondary phase
generation.structural_mediator: Grain refinement, introduction of lattice strains, or formation of a secondary phase
generation.mechanism: Increased homogeneity, grain refinement, and introduction of lattice strains leading to improved magnetic properties
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased coercivity (>100 Oe) and potentially improved saturation magnetization
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy with coercivity ≤ 100 Oe
generation.boundary: Limitations in grain size, lattice strain, and secondary phase formation
generation.uncertainty: Optimal HPT conditions, secondary phase composition, and grain size distribution for maximum coercivity improvement

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy samples with varying grain sizes and lattice strains using HPT. Measure coercivity and saturation magnetization using vibrating sample magnetometry (VSM) or superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) magnetometry.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the HPT-processed samples does not exceed 100 Oe, the hypothesis is falsified.
